doi:10.34133/research.0197.caption: A summary of 3D printing results of (A) hydrogel-based F127/LP inks and (B) polymer-based PCL/nHA inks with DCM as solvent. The number in the ink name refers to wt% for F127/LP inks and w/v% for PCL/nHA inks. The Barus effect (expansion of the inks exiting the nozzle) was observed at low-viscosity inks. The viscosity of inks increases with the concentrations of fillers LP and nHA; at too high viscosity, inks were unextrudable or clogged nozzle, and the printed filaments were prone to fracture. A higher SF of 3D printed filaments and 4-layer 0°/90° scaffold structure was achieved for 15F/8LP and PCL/20nHA inks.
